subject: Pilot top-up: staircase discount + conditional credit escrow?
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rojas <elena.rojas@cloudstride.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot top-up: staircase discount + conditional credit escrow?

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was great to work with. Quick note from our side on next steps: we heard you need a little more runway for the 6-week pilot and the procurement team is asking for a pricing approach that limits near-term spend while keeping conversion incentives aligned.

Two practical options we can offer:
- Timebox extension (additional 3 weeks) with a small flat top-up fee; or
- Credit-based runway with a staircase discount on committed consumption (higher discounts the more you convert during the pilot) plus the unused credits escrowed and refundable/redeployable on conversion.

Attached is a suggested price schedule (Price_Schedule_v3.xlsx) and a short escrow term sheet sketch. High-level ask: would CloudStride be open to the staircase + conditional-escrow approach? It lets you cap near-term cash outflow while giving us a fair path to convert based on measured usage.

If that sounds good I can loop in Finance to finalize numbers and Legal to prepare a short addendum.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com
(415) 555-0172

Attachments: Price_Schedule_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), Escrow_Termsheet.docx (term sheet)
From: Elena Rojas <elena.rojas@cloudstride.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudstride.com
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot top-up: staircase discount + conditional credit escrow?

Hi Priya — appreciate the options. Procurement likes the idea of limiting cash outlay, but they need two clarifications before we move forward: 

1) How does the escrow get released? Our legal wants objective triggers (conversion, go/no-go sign-off, or timeline expiry) rather than discretionary releases.
2) If we convert mid-pilot, how are already-used credits reconciled with the staircase discount?

If you can share a one-page flow (trigger -> action -> refund or conversion calculation), that will help speed procurement approval. Also include a DocuSign-ready addendum if possible — we try to avoid stand-alone manual approvals.

Best,
Elena
Elena Rojas
Head of ML Platform | CloudStride
elena.rojas@cloudstride.com

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot top-up: staircase discount + conditional credit escrow?

Hi Elena — thanks, totally fair asks. Proposal below (summary, I will push a one-pager + DocuSign addendum after you confirm structure):

- Escrow mechanics: CloudStride prepays X credits into a tri-party escrow account managed by a neutral custodian. Escrow release triggers (choose one):
  a) Conversion to a paid contract (credits applied at conversion with staircase discount applied retroactively to the period);
  b) Formal no-go sign-off at pilot close (unused credits refunded to CloudStride within 14 days); or
  c) Inactivity threshold after 45 days (partial refund pro-rated).

- Staircase discount: discounts apply on cumulative consumption thresholds across the pilot extension window. Example tiers (illustrative): 0-500k tokens = 0% discount, 500k-1M = 10%, 1M+ = 18%. If CloudStride converts, credits already consumed are re-priced at the applicable tier and the delta is reconciled (either credit top-up or invoice offset).

- Risk protections: Redwood will cap concurrency to agreed limits and provide token-level cost reporting for audit. Exact numbers in the SOW/Schedule.

I will attach a one-page flow and a DocuSign-ready addendum shortly. Marcus and Laura — can you confirm the refund window and whether Finance is okay with a tri-party escrow?

Thanks,
Priya
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 08:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot top-up: staircase discount + conditional credit escrow?

Priya — short answer: we can do the escrow but want two guardrails.

1) Refund SLA: 14 business days for any refundable balance after a no-go sign-off (ops to verify usage report).
2) Minimum refundable amount threshold: refunds only processed for balances > $2,500 to avoid heavy admin churn. Below that, we can issue account credit applied to future invoices.

Also recommend we avoid tri-party bank escrow for small pilots — instead use a mutual escrow agent (third-party custodian) with a capped fee paid by Redwood for pilots under $40k. If CloudStride is comfortable, we can include the escrow fee waiver in the initial addendum to smooth procurement.

Marcus
VP, Finance | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Thanks, everyone — this all looks reasonable. Procurement signaled they will accept:
- Tri-party escrow via a neutral custodian (Redwood to cover fee for pilots < $40k)
- 14 business day refund SLA; $2.5k minimum refundable threshold
- Staircase tiers as discussed (we’ll confirm exact token tiers with our engineers)

Next steps from CloudStride: we will sign the addendum via DocuSign once you send the DocuSign-ready file and the SOW with the concurrency caps. Please include the usage-report template and the final price schedule.

Elena
